title: Updated report of COVID-19 vaccine safety monitoring in Japan: Booster shots and paediatric vaccinations.
ehr_evidence: The data for this report are available to the public on the webpage (Japanese language only) of the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare of Japan.
summary: A descriptive pharmacovigilance safety monitoring report of COVID-19 mRNA vaccine booster (third) shots and paediatric (5-11 years) vaccinations in Japan from December 2021 to May 2022, reporting individual case adverse event rates.
key_findings: Among 40,923,719 third shots of BNT162b2 there were 1,585 (0.0039%) reports from healthcare professionals and 858 (0.0021%) from the MAH, lower than first and second shots.
Among 30,597,546 third shots of mRNA-1273 there were 712 (0.0023%) reports from healthcare professionals and 420 (0.0014%) from the MAH, also lower than first and second shots.
The overall reporting rate of serious adverse events associated with the third shot was generally lower than those for the first and second shots.
Reporting rates of myocarditis/pericarditis among young men with third shots tended to be higher than for first shots but lower than second shots.
No cases of death were confirmed by experts suggesting a causal relationship between vaccination and death (134 deduplicated BNT162b2 and 78 mRNA-1273 death reports).

In children aged 5-11 years, among 879,260 second shots there were 23 (0.0026%) reports from healthcare professionals and 16 (0.0018%) from the MAH, with one expert-confirmed pericarditis case (0.9 cases per 1 million shots).
captured_features: individual case safety reports (suspected adverse events)
number of shots administered (first, second, third)
study_design: pharmacovigilance safety monitoring report (descriptive, no control group)
population: Japanese national population; mRNA COVID-19 vaccine booster (third shot) recipients broadly from age 12 to 80+ and children aged 5-11 years, December 2021 to May 2022
exposure_domain: COVID-19 vaccination (mRNA vaccines BNT162b2 and mRNA-1273), booster and paediatric doses
limitations: Spontaneous adverse event reporting subject to underreporting and reporting bias.
No control/comparison group and reporting rates are not incidence, so causal inference is limited.
Mandatory reporting of myocarditis/pericarditis from December 2021 may have inflated reporting rates.
Cause of death varied widely and no causal relationship with vaccination was confirmed.
data_availability_statement: The data for this report are available to the public on the webpage (Japanese language only) of the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare of Japan ( https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/shingi/shingi-kousei_284075.html).
